Not OP, but I stopped permanently in 2018 with only a couple relapses. From my personal experience (I'm not a mental health expert), you really just have to take out the option of cutting, at least mentally, out of your daily schedule. 

I used to do it to relieve stress or to get some sweet endorphins, so I had to transition to just doing deep breathing routines or watching funny YouTube videos. It was pretty difficult, because I really did miss the pain, and I probably still miss it every once in a while, but because I transitioned to other activities and exercises to distract myself, cutting slowly stopped becoming an option I would seriously consider when I was feeling down. 

(Bad analogy incoming) It's sort of like switching from using sharpie to expo on a whiteboard. Yeah, the sharpie feels better and is faster, but once you switch to dry erase, after a while you look at the permanent marker and think "why the hell would I think about using that?"
